types.name: Visa-free visit
types.purpose: Tourism, visiting family or business meetings for nationalities that do not need an Irish visa (e.g. Serbia, the US, the EU).
types.who: Nationals who do not need an Irish visa
types.note: Up to 90 days, as stamped by the immigration officer at the border. Ireland is not in the Schengen area — days here do not count towards the 90/180 rule.

types.name: Short Stay 'C' visa
types.purpose: Visits of less than 90 days: tourism, family, business, short courses, conferences.
types.who: Nationals who need an Irish visa
types.maxValidity: Single or multiple entry, up to 5 years for frequent travellers
types.note: The border officer decides how long you may stay, at most 90 days.

types.name: British Irish Visa Scheme
types.purpose: One UK visa that also lets nationals of India and China travel to Ireland.
types.who: Nationals of India and China with a UK visa

types.name: Transit visa
types.purpose: Changing flights at an Irish airport — for the nationalities that need it.
types.who: Nationals who need a transit visa
types.note: Does not allow you to leave the airport.

types.name: Long Stay 'D' visa
types.purpose: Coming for more than 90 days to study, work or join family; you then register for a residence permission (Stamp).
types.maxValidity: Single entry; residence is then set by your Stamp

types.name: Critical Skills Employment Permit
types.purpose: Highly skilled jobs on the Critical Skills Occupations List, or other jobs above a high salary threshold.
types.who: Highly skilled workers with a job offer

types.name: General Employment Permit
types.purpose: Jobs not on the Ineligible Occupations List, with a labour market needs test.
types.maxValidity: Up to 2 years, renewable up to 3 more

types.name: Intra-Company Transfer Employment Permit
types.purpose: Senior managers, key staff and trainees moving to the Irish branch of their employer.
types.who: Staff of a company with an Irish branch

types.name: Dependant / Partner / Spouse Employment Permit
types.purpose: Spouses, partners and dependants of Critical Skills permit holders and some researchers.

types.name: Reactivation Employment Permit
types.purpose: People who fell out of the employment permit system through no fault of their own.
types.who: Former permit holders who lost status

types.name: Contract for Services Employment Permit
types.purpose: Employees of foreign companies working on a contract for an Irish company.

types.name: Internship Employment Permit
types.purpose: Full-time students at a third-level institution outside Ireland doing work experience.

types.name: Sport and Cultural Employment Permit
types.purpose: Work in sport or culture that adds to the quality of Irish sport and cultural life.

types.name: Exchange Agreement Employment Permit
types.purpose: Work under international exchange agreements, such as the Fulbright programme or AIESEC.

types.name: Working Holiday Authorisation
types.purpose: Young people (usually 18–30) from partner countries holidaying and working in Ireland.
types.maxValidity: Usually 12 months (2 years for some countries)

types.name: Student permission (Stamp 2 / 2A)
types.purpose: Full-time study on an approved course (Stamp 2); Stamp 2A for courses not on the list, no work.
types.maxValidity: Length of the course, with study time limits
types.note: Stamp 2 allows up to 20 hours of work a week in term time.

types.name: Third Level Graduate Programme (Stamp 1G)
types.purpose: Graduates of Irish third-level degrees looking for work.
types.maxValidity: 12 months (24 months after a master's or higher)

types.name: Stamp 0 — temporary stay without work
types.purpose: Retiring to Ireland, dependent adult relatives, visiting academics.
types.note: No work allowed. Not reckonable for citizenship.

types.name: Stamp 1 — work or business permission
types.purpose: Living in Ireland on an employment permit, business permission or working holiday.

types.name: Stamp 3 — family of a permit holder
types.purpose: Spouses, partners and children of employment permit holders and some researchers or religious ministers.

types.name: Stamp 4 — long-term residence
types.purpose: Living and working freely, e.g. after 2 years on a Critical Skills permit, spouses of Irish citizens, long-term residents.
types.who: Long-term residents and family of Irish citizens

types.name: Stamp 5 — without condition as to time
types.purpose: Residence without time limit after at least 8 years of lawful residence.
types.who: Residents with 8+ years of lawful residence
types.maxValidity: Without time limit (until the passport expires)

types.name: Investor and entrepreneur routes
types.purpose: Starting an innovative business (Start-up Entrepreneur Programme) or investing in Ireland.
types.note: The Immigrant Investor Programme closed to new applications in 2023.
